experiments.name: One-month-earlier pilot study
experiments.classification_rationale: A convenience-sample pilot is mentioned as informing the hypotheses; its design, randomization status, and results are not reported in the main article and are deferred to the appendix.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; comparison is across scored experiments, not across papers.
findings: The primary information experiment reports its logit table, model Ns, coefficients, standard errors, model-derived probabilities, confidence intervals, and robustness changes much more transparently than it reports assignment probabilities, exact stimuli, missingness, weights, or uncertainty construction.
The randomized question-order diagnostic reports only the existence and levels of randomization; it supplies no diagnostic outcome, estimator, sample by arm, effect, or uncertainty.
The pilot is inventory-only because the main article reports no pilot outcome or design details.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, Table 1, table notes, Figures 1–3, figure notes, and footnotes received equal evidentiary status. Full credit was awarded where these displays jointly resolved an item (for example, estimator, model Ns, effects, and uncertainty values). No credit was awarded for details merely pointed to in the appendix, preregistration, or replication materials.
checks: Table 1 and its note support logit estimation, coefficients, SE values, and Ns.
Figure notes connect plotted probabilities and ATE differences to Table 1 models.
Footnote 11 supports only the outcome coding it explicitly states; omitted park coding was not inferred.
Appendix pointers for stimuli, pilot results, balance, distributions, and robustness outputs were treated as absences in the main article.

rows.summary: ITT and analysis unit are explicit and clustered inference is described, but exact ICW construction, focal-specification mapping, missingness rules, multiplicity method, first-endline Ns, and complete numerical estimates/uncertainty are not reconstructable.
The respondent analysis unit and two 50/50 orders are clear, but no diagnostic estimand, model, analyzed sample, result, or inference is reported.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, tables, table notes, figures, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 2 supported intervention content; Figure 1 supported flow; Figure 3 and its note supported contrast and clustered 95% intervals; Tables 3–4 and notes supported follow-up N, estimates, SEs, fixed effects, and p-values. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display. Conversely, supplement pointers were treated only as evidence of main-article absence.

Tables 3–4 and notes read as main-article evidence for follow-up sample sizes, estimates, SEs, p-values, and fixed effects.

title: Improving Management with Individual and Group-Based Consulting: Results from a Randomized Experiment in Colombia
source_scope: Published main article only, including main-text Tables 1–6, Figures 1–3, notes and footnotes. Supplementary appendices, linked material, replication files, code and external sources were excluded.

experiments.name: Three-arm management-consulting field experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: This is the article's principal randomized evaluation: 159 firms were assigned within matched triplets to control, individual consulting, or group consulting and analyzed on management and firm outcomes.
experiments.design_label_note: The permitted label is used for an individually randomized ordinary treatment-control experiment; allocation was not unrestricted, because it was blocked in matched triplets with exactly one firm per arm.

direct_comparison.summary: Only AJPS055 was supplied. The randomized survey experiment is transparent about vignette content, outcome coding, group means, and key validity limitations, but not about allocation probabilities, exact estimand/estimator, per-cell Ns, inference construction, missingness rules, multiplicity, or numerical effect contrasts. Cross-paper synthesis is therefore deferred.

consistency_audit.finding: Main-text prose, Figures 1–2, figure notes, and footnotes were treated as equal evidence. Figure 1 earned full experimental-condition credit because its wording and note fully identify the manipulations. Figure 2 earned group-quantity and uncertainty-component credit. No deduction was made merely because evidence appeared in a display. Conversely, Footnote 7's pointer to Online Appendix B was not treated as supplying omitted regression details or numerical results.

title: Testing the Benefits of Public Deliberation

reviewed_pages.boundary_confirmation: All 16 supplied PDF pages are the published main article. PDF p.16 lists online appendices but contains no appendix content.

source_scope: Published main article only: PDF pages 1–16 (printed 319–334), including main-text figures, notes, and footnotes. Online supporting information, verification files, and all external sources were excluded.

experiments.name: Three-arm public-deliberation field experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: This is the article's central randomized experiment. Participants were assigned individually to Public Deliberation, Individual Deliberation, or information-only Control; all outcome, moderation, and robustness analyses reuse that assignment. The assignment mechanism, probabilities, stratification, and restrictions are too incompletely reported to support the more specific 'completely randomized experiment' label, and the intervention is not merely embedded in a survey.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text tables, figures, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes were treated as evidence on the same footing as prose. Missing details were not penalized merely for being absent from prose; they were scored missing only after checking relevant displays and notes. SI pointers did not supply omitted evidence.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment
direct_comparison.finding: No cross-paper ranking is possible in this one-paper session. Within EXP147, the randomized reduced-form analysis is strongest on condition reporting, analysis units, effect estimates, and validity discussion; it is weakest on outcome hierarchy/coding, participant-flow arm counts, complete missingness and multiplicity procedures, raw group quantities, and Table 10 traceability. The unscored structural model is less reproducible because equilibrium derivations, simulation details, model-fit displays, and bootstrap implementation are deferred or incompletely reported.

consistency_audit.status: passed with one table-note conflict flagged
consistency_audit.statement: Main-text tables and notes were treated as evidence on the same footing as prose. Table notes earned credit where they supplied coding, samples, controls, clustering, estimates, or uncertainty. Appendix pointers earned no credit for omitted content.
findings: Tables 3–9 supplied operative outcome, control, sample, coding, and standard-error details and were credited equally with prose.
Table 10's displayed long-run estimates were credited as effects with uncertainty and sample counts, but its mismatched note was not used to infer the missing long-run specification.
Figure 2 was credited as a plotted group trajectory but not as an exact numerical group-mean table.
Pointers to online Tables A.1–A.13 were recorded as pointers only, never as evidence that omitted details were reported.

title: Measuring Attitudes toward Public Spending Using a Multivariate Tax Summary Experiment

reviewed_pages.main_article_boundary: Entire 17-page PDF; journal article begins at PDF 1/printed 205 and references end at PDF 17/printed 221. No embedded appendix or supplement.

source_scope: Only article.pdf and its same-PDF text extractions were used. Supporting information, preregistration, Dataverse materials, code, external references, and web sources were excluded. Appendix pointers were treated only as evidence that details are absent from the main article.

experiments.name: October 2018 multivariate tax-summary choice experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: This is the article's main randomized survey experiment: each of 3,533 respondents received five randomly selected deficit-neutral proposal-versus-status-quo choice tasks. It is a survey experiment. The authors explicitly say it is not a traditional conjoint experiment, and the main article does not establish a standard completely randomized, factorial, cluster-randomized, or list-experiment assignment.

experiments.name: External validation survey of a fixed model-derived budget proposal
experiments.classification_rationale: A new YouGov UK-panel sample of 3,000 respondents answered one fixed comparison between the status quo and the model-derived proposal. The main article reports no randomized proposal or other randomized manipulation in this survey, so it is inventoried as an observational validation analysis and is not scored as an experiment.

additional_checklist.note: No additional checklist was supplied; no separate checklist assessment was performed.

findings: Main-text prose, equations, figures, figure notes, footnotes, and the Figure 1 prompt were given equal evidentiary status.
No regression table appears in the main article; graphical point estimates and posterior intervals in Figures 2–4 were credited as reported results.
Figure and note evidence earned credit where it made an element explicit; no score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display rather than prose.
Pointers to supporting information (proposal generation, model assumptions, checks, prompt, and further analyses) were not treated as supplying omitted information.
The Figure 1 note appears mismatched to the prompt (it refers to 'bottom five rows'); it was not used as experimental evidence.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.
direct_comparison.summary: For the scored primary experiment, design reporting is weakest because exact proposal generation, recruitment, and flow are absent. The structural estimand and graphical uncertainty reporting are comparatively strong, although missing priors and weighting details prevent full model reconstruction. No article-level score combines the primary experiment with the unscored observational validation survey.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, table notes, figure notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 2 earned credit for Ns, coefficients, outcome linkage, and column changes; Table 3 earned credit for factorial contrasts, period indicators, and specification changes. Neither table was credited for an estimator, uncertainty type, or dependence procedure that its text/note did not identify. Appendix/supporting-information pointers received no credit.
checks: Table 2 constant was accepted as the control mean in the unadjusted two-arm model.
Table 2 parenthetical values were not assumed to be standard errors because the note does not label them.
Table 3 reference contrasts and period indicators were credited from the display itself.
Table 3 parenthetical values, estimator, outcome, N, and clustering were not inferred from customary presentation.

title: A Choice-Based Measure of Issue Importance in the Electorate

reviewed_pages.boundary_basis: All 17 PDF pages are consecutively numbered published article pages. PDF page 17 ends with the article reference list and a Supporting Information availability list; no supporting-information content is embedded.

source_scope: Published main article only: main text, tables, figures, notes, and footnotes on PDF pages 1–17 (printed pp. 519–535). Supporting information, replication materials, and all external sources were excluded; pointers to them received no evidentiary credit.

experiments.name: Three-task hypothetical-candidate policy conjoint
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary randomized survey experiment producing the article’s core issue-importance estimates. Random issue/level assignment forms a conjoint with independently randomized candidate attributes; it is also a survey experiment. The response-option polarity randomization and diagnostic summaries are integral instrument/model checks, not separate samples or manipulations with separate outcome analyses.

experiments.name: Village-level PES randomized controlled trial with 2019 long-term follow-up
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary causal experiment. Villages were randomized to a PES offer or control; all 2019 behavioral and survey outcomes reuse that original assignment and therefore belong to this experiment. The one-winner-per-village seedling lottery only incentivized outcome elicitation and created no analyzed treatment contrast, so it is not inventoried as a separate experiment.

direct_comparison.note: This independent session contains one paper, so no between-paper winner or ranking is possible. The paper's primary experiment is strongest on reported estimates, uncertainty, raw group quantities, and validity discussion; it is weakest on treatment/randomization implementation, exact covariates and outcome coding, missingness, multiplicity, and reconstructable robustness details.

consistency_audit.statement: Tables, figure notes, table notes, prose, and footnotes received equal evidentiary status. Table 1 and its note earned credit for estimator, analysis N, fixed effects, weights, village clustering, estimates, and 95% CIs. Credit was withheld only where neither prose nor displays supplied the needed detail. Appendix pointers were not treated as evidence.
findings: Table 1 and its note were used directly for Criteria 7, 8, 10, 11, 14, 16, and 17; Criterion 7 still failed because the note omits Model 6's estimator.
Figure 1 and prose supplied group distributions/means; Table 3 supplied the displayed spillover robustness specification.

The table label 'stratification controls' plus prose identifying them as randomization strata established that assignment was stratified, while unnamed strata still failed the probability/restriction and covariate-detail components.
References to SI sections/tables did not supply omitted items, Lee bounds, robustness estimates, survey wording, or weight construction.

experiments.name: Pooled historical election-survey analyses (1984–2020)
experiments.classification_rationale: The article analyzes existing election surveys to relate measured RGC, resources, candidate context, and participation; no variable in this analysis is randomly assigned.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; cross-paper synthesis is deferred.

rows.comparison: Both omit allocation details, exact stimuli, complete flow, and outcome priority.
Analysis unit is clear; exact estimands, model operations, RGC construction, missingness, and inference details are not.
Both plot effects and 95% CIs and explain robustness checks; only Study 1 reports raw quantities for both outcomes.
Both discuss some limitations, but neither fully covers internal-validity threats or separates measured-RGC mechanism claims from the randomized contrast.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text prose, figures, figure notes, footnotes, and tables were treated as equal potential evidence. Figure 4 and Figure 5 earned credit for displayed point estimates and 95% confidence intervals. Missing implementation details were not inferred from conventional practice. Pointers to supplementary appendices and the Dataverse did not supply omitted information.

checks.detail: Graphical estimates, axes, legends, and notes were credited wherever they directly reported an item.
All cited Supplementary Appendix and Dataverse results were treated as unavailable unless summarized substantively in the main article.
OLS, conventional standard errors, balanced allocation, and complete-case analysis were not assumed.
Criterion scores are derived from component scores; component scores are not double-counted.

direct_comparison.summary: Both experiments disclose their unadjusted difference-in-means analyses well in tables and notes. E2 adds explicit meeting-clustered inference, while both share the same gaps in eligibility, flow, outcome priority, adjusted specifications, confidence-interval construction, missingness, multiplicity, robustness detail, and several internal-validity threats.

Conversely, pointers to supplementary tables and sections earned no credit for omitted details.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, tables, figure notes, table notes and footnotes were treated as equally eligible main-article evidence. Figure 3 supplied arm-specific raw quantities and outcome definitions.

direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper comparison only; cross-paper synthesis is deferred because this session contains one paper.
direct_comparison.summary: The main experiment and replication have the same transparency profile: strong condition descriptions, coding, sample sizes, raw means and coefficient/SE reporting, but incomplete allocation, estimator naming, repeated-measure inference, missingness, multiplicity and analysis-status reporting. The aggregated pilot series is not statistically reconstructable from the main article.

title: Non-Governmental Monitoring of Local Governments Increases Compliance with Central Mandates: A National-Scale Field Experiment in China
source_scope: Published main article only: all 18 PDF pages (printed pp. 626–643), including main text, Tables/Figures 1–4, their notes, and footnotes. PDF page 18 contains only a list of online supporting-information appendices; those appendices, replication materials, registration, cited external sources, and web links were not consulted as evidence.

experiments.name: Public disclosure of municipal PITI scores
experiments.classification_rationale: A new 50-city sample was randomly assigned to public disclosure or nondisclosure and formally analyzed as the article's central causal test. It is a completely randomized field experiment with matched-pair blocking; the prompt's design taxonomy has no separate field-experiment label. Follow-up PITI, online-attention, petition, and municipal-official interview outcomes use the original assignment and remain part of EXP1.

experiments.name: Local-NGO and local-scholar scope-condition interviews
experiments.classification_rationale: Seven NGOs using PITI and three local scholars were interviewed without randomized assignment. These qualitative scope-condition analyses are observational. The 20 municipal-official interviews are not listed separately because they are follow-up measurement under EXP1's original randomized city assignment.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, figures, tables, notes, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Table 1 supported component weights; Figure 2 and its note supported arm means, plotted effects, bootstrap SEs, and 90% blockwise-bootstrap intervals; Figures 3–4 and notes supported outcome-to-effect mapping and inference labels. No score was reduced merely because evidence appeared in a display, and no appendix pointer supplied omitted information.
checks: Equation 5 was accepted as a complete focal point estimator.
Figure notes were accepted for standard-error, confidence-level, and blockwise-bootstrap evidence.
Graphically reported estimates and intervals counted as reported results.
Pointers to SI Appendices A–J were treated only as pointers, not as evidence of their contents.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment
direct_comparison.statement: Only AJPS139 was supplied, so no cross-paper ranking is possible in this session. Within AJPS139, the primary experiment is strong on the explicit DID estimand and assignment-based test but weak on treatment replication, outcome coding, flow/N, resampling implementation, multiplicity, and alternative-specification detail.

Analysis unit: The reader can determine whether observations are participants, profiles, choices, sessions, or another unit.
Coding and reference categories: Treatment coding, outcome coding, omitted categories, and reference levels are explicit.
Specification: Covariates, fixed effects, weights, transformations, and column-to-column specification changes are explicit.
Dependence and inference: Standard errors, clustering, repeated-observation dependence, bootstrap or permutation procedures, and confidence-interval construction are explicit.
Missingness and attrition: Inclusion rules, missing outcomes, exclusions, attrition, and corresponding adjustments are explicit.
Multiplicity and analysis status: Multiple-testing procedures and prespecified versus exploratory analyses are distinguished.
Analysis sample: The number of observations used in each focal analysis is reported.
required_components: Analysis sample size for each focal analysis

core_criteria_catalog.wording: Group quantities: Relevant control means, treatment means, marginal means, or other raw quantities are reported.
Effect and uncertainty: Effect estimates and standard errors or confidence intervals are reported.
Model-to-result traceability: Each focal numerical result can be connected directly to a particular outcome, contrast, specification, sample, and inference procedure.
Robustness analyses: Alternative specifications and sensitivity analyses are explained sufficiently to understand what changed.
Internal-validity threats: Attrition, noncompliance, spillovers, demand effects, measurement problems, and other relevant threats are discussed.
Inferential scope: The paper distinguishes the randomized contrast from broader claims about mechanisms, populations, and settings.

findings: Main-text prose, Table 1, its title/subtitle, footnotes, and page footers were treated as eligible main-article evidence.
Table 1 was visually inspected and used to classify the fertility-rate summary as observational; it was not discounted because its evidence appears in a table.
The prose statement that the Matlab MCH/FP design was not randomized was given full evidentiary weight.
The pointer to the companion article and citations to prior work were not treated as supplying omitted design or statistical details.
No score was reduced for information being presented in a display rather than prose; there were simply no category 1–3 experiments to score.

subtitle: A field experiment provides a promising proof of concept

experiments.name: Three-arm behaviorally designed hiring-training field experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: This is the article's only new randomization and the basis of its headline claims. Hiring managers were assigned once to one of three arms; all outcome, subgroup, heterogeneity, and robustness analyses reuse that assignment.

experiments.name: Machine-learning analysis of 149 short-term team contests
experiments.classification_rationale: The article pools six contests from the focal study with 143 platform contests and applies a random-forest prediction analysis. The main article does not report randomized assignment for those 143 contests, so the pooled analysis is inventoried as observational rather than as 149 scored experiments.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent session; comparison is between the paper's scored experiments, not across papers.
direct_comparison.finding: The primary experiment is materially more transparent than the one-paragraph Dongguan summary: its main tables identify models, samples, estimates and standard errors. It still cannot be fully reconstructed because assignment probabilities, participant flow, missingness/attrition rules, some dependence details, raw group quantities, and supplement-derived robustness/headline analyses are absent. The Dongguan experiment supplies only a terse design sketch and one 12% result without an estimator or uncertainty.

consistency_audit.statement: Main-text tables and their notes were given the same evidentiary status as prose. Equations plus Tables 1–4 earned credit for estimand/model, analysis unit, coding, covariates, sample size, effect estimates and reported uncertainty. Scores were withheld only where the combined prose/table record remained incomplete (for example, Table 4's SE procedure and missing weighting status). SI pointers were treated as pointers, not evidence.

execution_record.original_model_output: This review.json is the original scored record generated in-session; no post hoc correction was applied.

experiments.name: Post-lockdown descriptive-norm × restaurant-certification field experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary randomized field experiment. Participants were individually blocked and independently assigned to descriptive-norm and certificate factors, creating a factorial design. The park procedure and moderator/measurement analyses use the same sample/assignment and are included here rather than counted as new experiments. The briefly named expanded prosocial-norm treatment is retained as an incompletely described attribute of this experiment because the main article does not establish a separate sample or assignment.

Table 5 supported preperiod quantities and analyzed counts; tables 6–8 and their notes supported outcome/contrast/sample/effect/t-statistic/p-value records. direct_comparison.scope: Within-paper experiment comparison only; this independent session contains one paper, so cross-paper synthesis is not possible here.
direct_comparison.finding: Study 1 and Study 2 have essentially the same main-article statistical transparency: both clearly identify estimands, OLS/within-person model families, analysis units, focal contrasts, estimates, and 95% CIs. Study 1 additionally reports longitudinal follow-up counts and a fixed-effects difference-in-differences approach; Study 2 uses a fresh unsensitized sample. Neither reports analysis-specific N, exact SE/CI construction, complete item coding, full stimulus/control content, or complete robustness results in the main article.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, figures, tables, table notes, and figure notes were given equal evidentiary status. experiments.name: First national survey list experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: A new national sample is randomized between a three-item control list and the same list plus the sensitive WWOH item, with a formal difference-in-means estimate and confidence interval.

design_map.value: National target of married Saudi men aged 18–35.

evidence.anchor: restricted the survey
evidence.paraphrase: The stated restriction is age, sex, nationality, and marriage; no other eligibility is supplied.

evidence.paraphrase: Only the recruiting organization is identified.

evidence.paraphrase: The lists, sensitive item, and response ranges are exact.

experiments.name: Surveyor recruitment social-norm information experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: A new sample of interested women is individually randomized to a company-support script with or without national support information; OLS and permutation analyses are reported.

design_map.label: Target population
design_map.value: Women aged 18–45 in a Saudi survey-company database across Jeddah, Riyadh, and Dammam who confirmed interest in a one-day at-home enumerator job.

evidence.anchor: confirmed their interest in the first call
evidence.paraphrase: The frame, cities, age range, and prior expression of interest are described.

design_map.label: Eligibility criteria
design_map.value: Female; age 18–45; in company database; confirmed interest in temporary at-home survey work. Other eligibility/exclusions NR.

evidence.anchor: 291 women, aged 18–45
evidence.paraphrase: Eligibility follows the two-call recruitment sequence.

design_map.label: Recruitment procedure
design_map.value: Company called its database, harmonized demographics, confirmed initial interest, then made a second call.

evidence.anchor: company first contacted women in their database
evidence.paraphrase: The recruitment sequence is explicit, but the initial number contacted is not.

design_map.label: Field dates and setting
design_map.value: January–February 2020; phone recruitment across three Saudi cities; one-day job in shopping malls or at home.

evidence.anchor: conducted in January and February 2020
evidence.paraphrase: Dates, cities, call setting, and work sites are stated.

design_map.label: Number recruited and analyzed
design_map.value: 291 offered the choice and analyzed in each Table 6 model; initial database/contact count and arm counts NR.

evidence.anchor: Observations 291
evidence.paraphrase: Table 6 gives the analysis N for every model.

design_map.label: Experimental arms or randomized attributes
design_map.value: Company-support message alone versus that message plus national-survey information that 82% of young married Saudi men support WWOH.

evidence.anchor: The other half ... were read
evidence.paraphrase: Both scripts are printed.

design_map.label: Unit of randomization
design_map.value: Individual woman.

evidence.anchor: at the individual level
evidence.paraphrase: The randomization unit is explicit.

design_map.label: Allocation probabilities and restrictions
design_map.value: One-half per arm; assignment algorithm, stratification, and restrictions NR.

evidence.anchor: One-half of the subjects
evidence.paraphrase: Equal allocation is stated; no implementation details follow.

design_map.label: Exact treatment and comparator
design_map.value: Control script: Vision 2030/company-support statement. Treatment adds the 82% support fact. Both then choose SAR200 at-home versus SAR240 plus transportation outside-home versions of the same one-day enumerator job.

evidence.anchor: performing the same enumerator job
evidence.paraphrase: The scripts, job variants, pay, and transportation are explicit.

design_map.label: Outcome definitions and timing
design_map.value: Two preregistered binary outcomes: chose outside-home offer on the second call; chose and showed up, from administrative data. Timing is immediate choice and subsequent one-day attendance.

evidence.anchor: two (pre-registered) outcomes
evidence.paraphrase: Definitions, status, and data sources are stated.

design_map.label: Estimand
design_map.value: Average effect of information assignment on outside-home sign-up and show-up indicators.

evidence.anchor: on the treatment indicator
evidence.paraphrase: Table 6 defines each treatment coefficient.

design_map.label: Estimator or statistical model
design_map.value: OLS indicator-on-treatment regressions; adjusted columns add five listed socioeconomic controls.

evidence.anchor: Columns 1 and 3 report estimates from OLS
evidence.paraphrase: The table note reconstructs all four models.

design_map.label: Analysis unit
design_map.value: Individual woman.

evidence.anchor: whether the respondent signed up
evidence.paraphrase: Outcomes and regressions are respondent-level.

design_map.label: Variable coding and reference categories
design_map.value: Treatment = support-information script; omitted control = company-support-only script; both outcomes are binary indicators.

evidence.anchor: on the treatment indicator
evidence.paraphrase: Scripts identify arm coding and the table note identifies binary outcomes.

design_map.label: Covariates and fixed effects
design_map.value: Columns 1/3 unadjusted; columns 2/4 control for age, marital status, children, education, and employment. No fixed effects, weights, or transformations reported.

evidence.anchor: include socioeconomic controls for age
evidence.paraphrase: The exact covariates and column changes are stated.

design_map.label: Standard-error and inference procedure

title: Sleep preferentially consolidates negative aspects of human memory: Well-powered evidence from two large online experiments

main_article_boundary.boundary_basis: The PDF is a continuous 8-page PNAS article numbered 1 of 8 through 8 of 8. Materials and Methods end on page 7; page 8 contains references. No supplementary appendix pages are embedded.

source_scope: Published main article only: PDF pages 1–8, including main-text figures and notes. Page 8 was reviewed as references only. Online SI, OSF data, code, preregistration/registries, and external methodological sources were not consulted or credited.

experiments.name: Experiment 1: negative emotional memory trade-off
experiments.classification_rationale: A separate eligible sample was randomized within age ranges to a sleep or wake delay, and the central negative-memory hypothesis received formal 2 × 2 × 2 mixed-factorial ANOVA analysis. Because assignment was age-stratified, the stricter completely-randomized label is not applied.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment
direct_comparison.finding: Cross-paper comparison is not possible in this session. Within the article, all four country experiments have the same transparency profile because methods and displays are reported jointly. Country-specific sample sizes, dates, nationality levels, and work-history levels differ, but the same omissions affect all four.

findings: Table 1 and its notes received the same evidentiary weight as prose for attribute levels, country-specific nationality variants, work-history variants, and reference categories.
Figures 1–6 and their notes received full evidentiary weight for displayed marginal means, AMCEs, subgroup/interaction mappings, and visible error bars.
No credit was given for the meaning or level of error bars because neither figure notes nor prose defines them.

experiments.name: MTurk magnitude-manipulation pretest
experiments.classification_rationale: The article explicitly calls this a pretest experiment used to select ratio wording. It reports only qualitative pilot conclusions, with no numerical outcome or formal analysis.

experiments.name: Pretreatment observational survey of trade beliefs and predispositions
experiments.classification_rationale: The pretreatment survey measured trade attitudes, social dominance, empathy, and preexisting zero-sum beliefs without randomized assignment of those characteristics; descriptive proportions and experimental-effect moderation use these observational measures.

direct_comparison.scope: Single-paper independent assessment; comparison is across the paper's experiments, not across papers.
direct_comparison.finding: The US and Canadian factorial experiments have identical reporting structures and scores. Their randomized contrasts and analysis unit are clear, but their models, inference procedures, analysis-specific Ns, and numerical effects are not reconstructable from the main article. The two question-order randomizations disclose only the randomized order and have no reported analysis.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, figures, figure notes, table-equivalent displays, and footnotes were given equal evidentiary status. Figure 9 completed the seven-level magnitude list and supported criterion 2. Figures 1–8 supported identification of outcomes/contrasts and p-value claims. They did not earn estimator, inference, or numerical-effect credit because axes/error bars and notes omit those details and refer the models to excluded Appendix B. No main-text tables were present.

title: Can Social Contact Reduce Prejudice and Discrimination? Evidence from a Field Experiment in Nigeria

reviewed_pages.boundary_finding: The 24-page PDF is the continuous published article from title/abstract through references. The supplementary-material notice on PDF page 22 is only a pointer; no appendix pages are embedded.

source_scope: Only article.pdf and its same-PDF extractions article.txt/pages.json were used. Online appendices, preregistration, registry, replication materials, external references, and web sources were not consulted or credited.

experiments.name: UYVT multi-stage randomized field experiment
experiments.classification_rationale: Primary experiment: the article's central design randomly assigns program access, then class religious composition, then partner religion within the same sampled cohort and presents three nested primary contrasts.

design_map.label: Target population
design_map.value: Young Christian and Muslim men aged 18–25 living in the poorest, previously violent neighborhoods within one hour of central Kaduna.

design_map.value: Male; age 18–25; resident of sampled residential EAs in 16 selected poor, violence-affected Kaduna neighborhoods; article frames sample as Christian or Muslim.

title: How Experiments Help Campaigns Persuade Voters: Evidence from a Large Archive of Campaigns’ Own Experiments

reviewed_pages.boundary_confirmation: All 19 PDF pages are the published main article. Pages 17–19 contain declarations/references; no supplement is embedded. Appendix, Dataverse, PAP, and replication links were not followed.

source_scope: Published main article only, including main-text tables, figures, notes, and footnotes; external supplementary material, PAPs, Dataverse files, and references excluded.
inventory_note: The article states there are 146 distinct randomized survey experiments but does not enumerate them. E001–E146 are synthetic preservation indices, not article study IDs. Shared scores reflect the same main-article reporting gap for every unnamed experiment.

experiments.name: Archive randomized survey experiment 001 (synthetic inventory index; study identity not reported)
experiments.classification_rationale: One of the 146 randomized survey experiments forming the article's primary evidence. The main article does not enumerate or identify studies, so this index preserves distinct units without pretending to recover study identity. It cannot be mapped to the 2018 cluster scheme or 2020 individual scheme.

design_map.label: Target population
design_map.value: NR for the individual experiment; clients targeted either the entire U.S. or selected states.

evidence.anchor: the entire US or just select states
evidence.paraphrase: Campaign clients specified either a national or selected-state population, but the article does not map a geography to each experiment.

design_map.label: Eligibility criteria
design_map.value: NR for the individual experiment; archive-level inclusion required candidate-persuasion video with audio, supporting a Democrat and/or opposing a Republican.

evidence.anchor: restricted to ‘candidate persuasion’ videos
evidence.paraphrase: The archive excludes issue-only and turnout-only ads and, on the next page, static, text-only, and no-audio treatments.

design_map.label: Recruitment procedure
design_map.value: Online through Swayable's proprietary acquisition channels; operational procedure NR.

evidence.anchor: recruited subjects online through their proprietary acquisition channels
evidence.paraphrase: Recruitment is described only as online recruitment through proprietary channels; source panels, invitations, and eligibility screening are not given.

design_map.label: Field dates and setting
design_map.value: NR for the individual experiment; online survey setting within archive windows 2018-04-04–2019-03-15 or 2019-12-07–2020-12-24.

evidence.anchor: between April 4, 2018 and March 15, 2019
evidence.paraphrase: The article gives archive-level field windows for 2018 and 2020, not a date for each unnamed experiment.

design_map.label: Number recruited and analyzed
design_map.value: NR; only three dataset-level totals are reported.

evidence.paraphrase: Table 1 reports aggregate N values of 93,969, 101,782, and 302,589 for the three datasets, but no N for each experiment.

evidence.anchor: Full study-level tables are available in Dataverse Appendix DA1
evidence.paraphrase: The article explicitly places the study-level summaries in excluded external material.

design_map.label: Experimental arms or randomized attributes
design_map.value: NR for the individual experiment; campaign video-ad arms versus one placebo video, with 618 aggregate Table 1 treatments and no study-level mapping.

evidence.anchor: randomized into treatment conditions or a placebo
evidence.paraphrase: Treatments were campaign video ads; the comparator was a non-electoral public-service video that varied by study. The exact videos are not listed by experiment.

evidence.anchor: Full study-level tables are available in Dataverse Appendix DA1
evidence.paraphrase: The article explicitly places the study-level summaries in excluded external material.

design_map.label: Unit of randomization
design_map.value: NR for the individual experiment; 2018 used entry-time clusters and 2020 used individuals.

evidence.anchor: in the 2018 data, treatments were cluster-assigned
evidence.paraphrase: 2018 assignment used 1–4 minute entry-time clusters; 2020 assignment was individual with dynamically updating probabilities. The article does not identify which unnamed experiment used which scheme.

design_map.label: Allocation probabilities and restrictions
design_map.value: NR; dynamic targets/probabilities are described but exact 2020 probabilities were not saved, and the individual experiment is not mapped to a scheme.

evidence.anchor: these assignment probabilities were not saved
evidence.paraphrase: The 2020 probabilities are expressly unavailable; eleven studies also changed arms and were truncated by the analysts.

design_map.label: Exact treatment and comparator
design_map.value: NR; ad identity and the study-varying public-service placebo identity are omitted.

evidence.anchor: randomized into treatment conditions or a placebo
evidence.paraphrase: Treatments were campaign video ads; the comparator was a non-electoral public-service video that varied by study. The exact videos are not listed by experiment.

evidence.anchor: Full study-level tables are available in Dataverse Appendix DA1
evidence.paraphrase: The article explicitly places the study-level summaries in excluded external material.

design_map.label: Outcome definitions and timing
design_map.value: Post-treatment vote choice and/or favorability, initially 0–10 and rescaled to 0–100; exact items, outcome set, and primary/secondary status NR by experiment.

evidence.anchor: two post-treatment outcome measures, vote choice and favorability
evidence.paraphrase: Outcomes were initially 0–10, rescaled to 0–100; multi-item measures became weighted indices. Which outcome(s) belong to each experiment is not reported.

evidence.anchor: create a vote choice (or favorability) index as weighted average
evidence.paraphrase: Footnote 5 specifies sign reversal and averaging rules for candidate and opponent items.

design_map.label: Estimand
design_map.value: Average treatment effect of each ad versus the common placebo on the relevant outcome.

evidence.anchor: average treatment effect estimates
evidence.paraphrase: The plotted first-stage quantity is each ad’s average treatment effect relative to the common placebo on vote choice or favorability.

design_map.label: Estimator or statistical model
design_map.value: OLS of outcome on ad indicators and available pretreatment covariates; exact experiment specification NR.

evidence.anchor: ordinary least squares regressions of the outcome on indicators for each treatment

design_map.label: Analysis unit
design_map.value: Participant/respondent for first-stage ad effects; ad-level estimates for meta-analysis.

evidence.anchor: ordinary least squares regressions of the outcome on indicators for each treatment
evidence.paraphrase: The first-stage estimator is OLS with treatment indicators and available pretreatment covariates, but the exact covariate set varies by study and is not mapped.

evidence.anchor: random-effects meta-analyses

direct_comparison.paper: EXP169 — Religious Divisions and Production Technology: Experimental Evidence from India
direct_comparison.summary: Equations and table notes make the core linear regressions unusually traceable, but missing-data rules, complete flow, multiplicity/status, arm-specific raw quantities, and resampling implementation prevent full reconstruction.

consistency_audit.statement: Prose, equations, tables, figures, table/figure notes, and footnotes in the main article received equal evidentiary status. Tables 2–6 earned credit where their headings, rows, and notes supplied coding, analysis unit, fixed effects, sample size, estimates, and clustered uncertainty. Appendix citations earned no credit for omitted details or results.
examples: Table 2 note established treatment coding, analysis unit, clustering, estimates, and bootstrap intervals.
Tables 3–5 notes established analysis units, coding, fixed effects, observation counts, and clustered standard errors.
A pointer to Table B.14 did not supply missing attrition rules; pointers to Tables B.15–B.21 did not supply excluded resampling results.
